prompt: Three weeks were missed by +100, −200 and +300 orders. What is the MAE, in orders?
The same three errors, +100, −200 and +300. What is the bias, in orders?
The same three errors, +100, −200 and +300. What is the RMSE, in orders, to one decimal place?
hint: Square, average, square root: (10,000 + 40,000 + 90,000) / 3, then the root.

prompt: A forecast's RMSE is much larger than its MAE. What does that say?

choices.text: The forecast is biased upwards
choices.why: Neither MAE nor RMSE has a sign; bias is a separate number.

choices.text: A few misses were much bigger than the rest
choices.why: Right. Squaring lets the big ones dominate.

choices.text: The computation is wrong, since RMSE should equal MAE when the forecast is unbiased
choices.why: They are equal only when every miss has the same size, bias or not.

choices.text: The series is small
choices.why: Both are in the same units, so size moves them together.

prompt: Why print the bias beside the accuracy measures?

choices.text: It is the one error a subtraction removes
choices.why: Right. A forecast wrong in the same direction every week is the most fixable kind.

choices.text: It replaces MAE when the series is large
choices.why: It complements MAE; errors can average to zero while being large.

choices.text: Bias is what MAPE measures, expressed in orders instead of in per cent of the actual week
choices.why: MAPE drops the signs; bias keeps them.

choices.text: A bias of zero proves the forecast is good
choices.why: Huge misses in both directions can cancel to zero.

prompt: Why did the seasonal naive forecast do so badly on Panela's first half of 2025?

choices.text: Seasonal naive is always a poor method
choices.why: On a series without growth it is often the one to beat.

choices.text: Carnival moved
choices.why: That costs it a couple of weeks, not every week.

choices.text: It was fitted on too few weeks
choices.why: It is not fitted at all; it repeats last year.

choices.text: The business had grown about a fifth since the year it repeats
choices.why: Right. Its bias was large and negative.

prompt: Seasonal ARIMA has MAE 362.0 and RMSE 501.8; Holt-Winters has MAE 366.0 and RMSE 462.3. A badly missed week means customers left without boxes. Which model fits that cost better?

choices.text: Seasonal ARIMA, because it has the smaller MAE
choices.why: MAE treats a big miss like several small ones, which is not this cost.

choices.text: Neither, since they differ by less than one per cent
choices.why: Their MAEs do; their RMSEs differ by about 40 orders, and that is the measure that matches the cost.

choices.text: Holt-Winters
choices.why: Right. Its smaller RMSE means fewer large misses, and large misses are what cost here.

choices.text: Whichever has the lower MAPE
choices.why: MAPE is a scaled MAE and inherits its blindness to big misses.

prompt: Holt-Winters had a bias of about +200 orders a week over 26 weeks. Roughly how many orders too many did it forecast in total? Answer to the nearest hundred.
A forecast of 100 misses by 50 in both directions on two different weeks. Why does MAPE score the two misses differently?

choices.text: It counts over-forecasts twice
choices.why: It counts each once; the denominator differs.

choices.text: It divides by the actual, which is 150 in one week and 50 in the other
choices.why: Right: 33 per cent and 100 per cent.

choices.text: It squares the errors first
choices.why: That is RMSE.

choices.text: It does not: both are 50 per cent
choices.why: That would be dividing by the forecast, which MAPE does not.

prompt: A product sells two or three a day and none on some days. Which measure should not be used for its forecasts?

choices.text: MAPE
choices.why: Right. A day with no sales cannot be divided by.

choices.text: MAE
choices.why: MAE handles zeros fine.

choices.text: WAPE, the total absolute error over the total actual
choices.why: WAPE only fails if every day is zero.

choices.text: RMSE
choices.why: RMSE handles zeros fine too.

prompt: A team picks its forecasting model by lowest MAPE. In which direction will its choices tend to lean?

choices.text: Towards models that forecast high
choices.why: The opposite: high misses happen on quieter weeks and count more.

choices.text: Towards the most complex model, since MAPE rewards parameters
choices.why: MAPE knows nothing about parameters.

choices.text: Neither: MAPE is symmetric by construction
choices.why: The lesson's two weeks show it is not.

choices.text: Towards models that forecast low
choices.why: Right. A low miss is divided by a larger actual.

prompt: A manager wants to compare forecast quality between Panela's Southeast and its much smaller North. Which measure allows that, if the North has no zero days?

choices.text: RMSE, because it punishes big misses
choices.why: It is in orders, so the Southeast would always look worse.

choices.text: MAE, as long as both are measured over the same weeks
choices.why: Same weeks do not remove the difference in scale.

choices.text: MAPE
choices.why: Right. It is the only one of the three free of the series' size.

choices.text: Bias
choices.why: Bias is in orders too, and measures direction, not size.

prompt: Four days had actual sales 3, 1, 0 and 2, and the forecast was 2 every day. What is the WAPE, the total absolute error over the total actual, in per cent?
Why measure a forecast from several starting weeks rather than one?

choices.text: To give the fitting more data, because each extra origin adds weeks to the training set
choices.why: Each origin uses less data, not more.

choices.text: Another start brings other holidays and another winner
choices.why: Right. In the lesson each model won three of six origins.

choices.text: It is faster
choices.why: It refits the model at every origin, which is slower.

choices.text: statsmodels requires it
choices.why: Nothing requires it but honesty.

prompt: An analyst fits a model once on all three years, then measures its error on each quarter of 2025. What is wrong?

choices.text: The model saw 2025 while being fitted
choices.why: Right. Each origin must be fitted only on data before it.

choices.text: Quarters are too long a test
choices.why: Length is fine; what the model saw is not.

choices.text: Nothing, if the model is Holt-Winters, because its weights only look backwards in time
choices.why: The parameters were chosen using 2025, so 2025 is not a test.

choices.text: 2025 contains a price rise
choices.why: That makes the test harder, not invalid.

prompt: Two models tie on a rolling evaluation. Which of these is a reasonable way to choose?

choices.text: Pick the one with more parameters
choices.why: Parameters are cost, not quality.

choices.text: Re-run the comparison on the test weeks, adjusting each model until one of them wins
choices.why: That turns the test into training.

choices.text: Always the newer method, because newer methods have learnt from the mistakes of older ones
choices.why: Competitions repeatedly find simple and old methods hard to beat.

choices.text: The one the team will keep running, or both averaged
choices.why: Right. When accuracy ties, other things decide.

prompt: Match each measure to what it is.

pairs.right: the root of the average squared miss
the average miss as a share of the actual
the average miss, keeping its sign

prompt: Put the steps of an honest forecast comparison in order.
items: fix the test weeks and the horizon
fit each model only on data before each origin
forecast the test weeks from every origin
compute the same measures for every model, baselines included

prompt: The measure that divides the total absolute error by the total actual, and survives days with zero sales, is called ___.
Panela's RMSE of 462 orders a week is reported to a board as 'an error of 462'. What context is missing?

choices.text: The MAPE of the baseline
choices.why: Useful, but the first thing missing is the scale of 462 itself.

choices.text: The model's parameters
choices.why: A board does not need alpha to judge an error.

choices.text: How big a typical week is: nine to eleven thousand
choices.why: Right. RMSE is in the series' units and means nothing without its scale.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: 462 is good for ten thousand and terrible for five hundred.
